categories.label: Felony assault
categories.short: An attack causing serious injury, or any injury with a weapon
categories.plain: An attack that causes serious injury, or any injury caused with a weapon, or an injury to a police officer, transit worker, nurse or other protected worker on the job.

categories.label: Robbery
categories.short: Taking property from someone by force or threat of force
categories.plain: Forcible stealing: taking property from a person by using or threatening immediate physical force.

categories.label: Murder
categories.short: Killing a person; includes non-negligent manslaughter
categories.plain: Killing a person intentionally or through conduct showing depraved indifference to human life; NYPD’s count also includes non-negligent manslaughter.
categories.caveat: Small numbers; most years are in single digits.

categories.label: Misdemeanor assault
categories.short: An attack causing an injury the law doesn’t count as serious
categories.plain: An attack that causes an injury the law doesn’t count as ‘serious’: real pain or harm, like a punch that leaves bruises or a bloody nose.

categories.label: Burglary
categories.short: Entering a building illegally to commit a crime
categories.plain: Entering or staying in a building unlawfully with intent to commit a crime there.

categories.label: Grand larceny
categories.short: Theft over $1,000, or of items like a credit card
categories.plain: Theft of property worth more than $1,000, or of certain items, such as a credit card, regardless of value; NYPD counts stolen cars separately, as vehicle theft.
categories.caveat: Includes some card and identity theft logged where the victim reported it.
categories.mapNote: Large clusters at stores are mostly shoplifting, by NYPD’s own offense codes.

categories.label: Vehicle theft
categories.short: Stealing a car, truck, motorcycle or other vehicle
categories.plain: Stealing a car, truck, motorcycle or other motor vehicle (grand larceny of a motor vehicle).

categories.label: Felony criminal mischief
categories.short: Damaging someone’s property, causing over $250 in damage
categories.plain: Intentionally damaging someone else’s property, causing more than $250 in damage.

countsOnly.label: Rape
countsOnly.short: Sex without consent; since Sept. 2024, includes oral and anal sex
countsOnly.plain: Sexual intercourse without consent, including by force or with someone who can’t legally consent; since Sept. 1, 2024, the law also counts forced oral and anal sex as rape.
countsOnly.why: NYPD records every rape report at the precinct station house to protect victims, so locations can’t be mapped.
countsOnly.notComparable: New York broadened its legal definition of rape on Sept. 1, 2024: forced oral and anal sex, previously charged as ‘criminal sexual act,’ now count as rape. So 2025 rape and sex-crime counts aren’t comparable with 2019.

countsOnly.label: Felony sex crimes
countsOnly.short: Felony sexual offenses other than rape
countsOnly.plain: Felony sexual offenses other than rape, such as first-degree sexual abuse; before Sept. 1, 2024, this also included forced oral and anal sex, then charged as ‘criminal sexual act.’
countsOnly.why: Like rape, NYPD places these reports at the station house, so they can’t be mapped.
countsOnly.notComparable: New York broadened its legal definition of rape on Sept. 1, 2024: forced oral and anal sex, previously charged as ‘criminal sexual act,’ now count as rape. So 2025 rape and sex-crime counts aren’t comparable with 2019.

countsOnly.label: Forgery, theft-fraud and identity theft
countsOnly.short: Forgery, theft by deception and identity theft
countsOnly.plain: Forging documents or money, stealing through fraud or deception, and using someone else’s identity, when charged as a felony.
countsOnly.why: Often reported where the victim lives or banks, not where the crime happened.

countsOnly.label: Felony drug offenses
countsOnly.short: Selling drugs, or possessing larger amounts
countsOnly.plain: Felony drug offenses, such as selling drugs or possessing them in larger amounts or with intent to sell.
countsOnly.why: Mostly arrests made by police, so the numbers track enforcement as much as crime.

countsOnly.label: Felony weapons offenses
countsOnly.short: Such as carrying a loaded gun without a license
countsOnly.plain: Felony weapon offenses, such as carrying a loaded gun without a license.
countsOnly.why: Mostly arrests made by police, so the numbers track enforcement as much as crime.

countsOnly.label: Hate crimes
countsOnly.short: Crimes motivated by bias against a group
countsOnly.plain: Crimes that NYPD’s Hate Crime Task Force confirmed were motivated, in whole or in part, by bias against a person’s race, religion, sexual orientation or another protected trait.
countsOnly.why: NYPD publishes hate crimes by precinct only, not by location. They overlap with other categories (a hate-motivated assault is also counted as an assault).

countsOnly.label: Criminal contempt (felony)
countsOnly.short: Serious violations of orders of protection
countsOnly.plain: First-degree criminal contempt: a serious violation of a court order of protection, such as one involving a threat, physical contact or a repeat violation.
countsOnly.why: Mostly violations of court orders of protection, which are about a person, not a place.

precincts.name: 5th Precinct
notes: 75 of this precinct’s 301 felony assault reports in 2025 are mapped to a single location, near the Manhattan Detention Complex and the criminal courthouse at 100 Centre St. Unlike crimes inside city jails, these reports are included in the precinct’s official totals. In 2019, 62 of 214 reports were mapped near the same buildings; the official 2019 total was 163.

precincts.name: 41st Precinct
notes: Until 2014, NYPD counted crimes reported in city jails in precinct totals. This precinct’s felony assaults fell from 732 in 2013 to 353 in 2014, when they were split out, so its trend lines start in 2014.
157 of this precinct’s 544 felony assault reports in 2025 (and 126 of 394 in 2019) are mapped at or next to the Vernon C. Bain Center, a city jail.
